I'm 54, been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou since I was 24 when my father handed me the land. I only finished primary school — I can read a newspaper headline and write my name, but that's about it. Everything I know about farming I learned from my father and from watching my neighbors. We've got 7 people under our roof: me, my wife, my old mother, my son and his wife, and their two kids. My son works at a factory over in Handan and only comes back for planting and harvest. My daughter-in-law helps my wife with the cotton picking in autumn.

I split my 8 mu into two pieces. Six mu I do wheat-maize double crop — that's my main food and income. The other two mu I plant cotton. The cotton gives us cash, and my wife and my mother can pick it slow over the autumn months.

Right now it's late April. My wheat went in last October after the National Day holiday, same as every year. I used my own saved seed — I've been saving it for years, it's good strong wheat, no need to waste money buying new seed every year. Back in October I put down base fertilizer: about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's about 50 jin (25 kg). Now the wheat is at jointing, looking pretty green. My neighbor Old Zhang already topdressed his wheat last week, so I need to do mine too. I'll put down about 20 jin of urea per mu (10 kg) this week. If it doesn't rain in the next few days, I'll run the pump once — the water costs money, about 15 yuan each time, but the wheat needs it at this stage. I already irrigated once at green-up in March. So that's two times so far, and maybe one more at grain filling if June is dry. For pesticide, I sprayed herbicide in early spring, and I'll watch for aphids. If I see them, I'll spray some insecticide.

For cotton, I'm planting it now on the 2 mu. I buy hybrid cotton seed from the seed shop in town — costs about 50 yuan per mu. Before planting I put down base fertilizer: about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. I'll plant by hand, row by row, me and my wife. Later in July when it flowers, I'll topdress with some urea, maybe 20 jin per mu. I'll irrigate once or twice depending on the rain — probably once in July and once in August if it's dry. Cotton always has bollworms, so I'll spray insecticide 3-4 times over the summer.

For maize, I can't plant until I harvest the wheat in early June. The window is tight — sometimes only 5-7 days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I hire a combine for the wheat harvest, costs about 50 yuan per mu. Then I need to get the maize in quick. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 40 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the rows at planting, about 40 jin per mu, and when the maize is knee-high I topdress with urea, about 30 jin per mu. Maize doesn't always need much irrigation — if the summer rains are good, maybe once or not at all. But if it's dry in July, I'll run the pump once. I expect about 900 jin per mu (around 450 kg) for maize if the weather is normal.

Money is always tight. This year I've got about 2,500 yuan saved up for inputs. The seed for cotton and maize costs me about 340 yuan. Fertilizer is the big expense — I need compound and urea for all three crops, that's over 1,000 yuan. Irrigation pumping costs another few hundred. Pesticides maybe 300 yuan. And I need to pay for the combine at wheat harvest. That leaves me with almost nothing spare, but I can manage. My son sends some money from Handan when he can, but I don't like to ask — he has his own family to feed. So I buy the fertilizer that's on sale at the cooperative, and I don't hire labor if I can avoid it. My wife and I do most of the work, with help from my daughter-in-law and my mother. We might hire a couple of days of labor at wheat harvest if we're running behind, but I'd rather save that money.
